column1: # services.tsv -- the units this setup turns on, and the one it turns off.
# Format: scope <TAB> unit <TAB> action
#   scope   system  systemctl (needs sudo)
#           user    systemctl --user
#   action  enable   enable --now, if the unit exists on this machine
#           disable  disable --now, but only if it is currently enabled or
#                    active -- so a machine that never had it stays quiet
# A unit that does not exist is skipped without comment: these are all provided
# by packages.tsv, and a missing one is already reported by the package step.
# Backends behind the launcher providers. Installing the package is not enough:
# nmcli, bluetoothctl and powerprofilesctl all talk to a daemon.
system
system
system
# Noctalia's idle service is what this repo configures (70-idle.toml). hypridle
# does the same job from a config directory the repo does not manage, and on a
# machine that ran ~/repos/dots it is still enabled as a user unit -- so the
# screen locks on whichever of the two counts down first, with two different
# sets of timeouts and only one of them written down here.
# A user unit, so no sudo, and disabling it is a one-word undo if you would
# rather keep hypridle: `systemctl --user enable --now hypridle`, and then set
# every behaviour in 70-idle.toml to enabled = false so only one of them acts.
# See docs/decisions/006-idle-has-one-owner.md.
user
